content.title: Where to watch WrestleMania 42 and catch all the incredible matches on this card
content.text: Cody Rhodes defeats Solo Sikoa In The Bloodline Rules Match For The Undisputed WWE Championship during the WWE SummerSlam at Cleveland Browns stadium. Joshua Gunter, cleveland.comIf you purchase a product through a link on our site, we may receive compensation.By Ben Axelson | baxelson@syracuse.comCody Rhodes vs. Randy Orton. CM Punk vs. Roman Reigns. It’s all finally happening when WWE WrestleMania 42 arrives after months of anticipation. Fans can stream the whole thing for free if they sign up for a 5-day free trial of fuboTV, or similar streaming offer. We’ve broken down all your streaming options below, and made our pick for your best place to stream WrestleMania 42 this weekend.What is WrestleMania 42 streaming on?WrestleMania 42 will air exclusively on ESPN streaming apps, with expanded coverage on ESPN2, which means you can stream it on any streaming service that includes access to ESPN Unlimited content, including fuboTV (free trial), DIRECTV (free trial) or ESPN Unlimited.We recommend fuboTV as the best streaming service for WWE WrestleMania 42, both for its five-day free trial and better-than-the-competition monthly pricing.Fans who access ESPN via a different streaming service will still need to authenticate their access via ESPN, and stream via ESPN apps.fuboTV free trialFuboTV is a live TV streaming service focused on live sports, including U.S. and international soccer, the NFL, MLB, NBA, NHL and more. It also includes its own fubo Sports Networks with exclusive programming, and includes ESPN networks and ESPN Unlimited in its base pricing. It offers 200+ channels starting at $73.99, including unlimited hours of DVR, and streams on most devices. Right now you can try fuboTV free for 5 days then take $25 off your first month of service.fuboTV$73.99$48.99Stream local and national sports with your free trial of fuboTV, and get $25 off your first month.Start for freeDIRECTV free trialDIRECTV has live TV from major broadcast and popular cable networks, including ESPN Unlimited access. Enjoy local and national live sports, breaking news, and must-see shows the moment they air. DIRECTV also has a five-day free trial, but its entry-level Entertainment package is $89.99 per month. However, fans can sign up for the expanded channel Choice package ($94.99 per month) and get $35 off their first month of service for just $59.99. The advantage to DIRECTV is the inclusion of NBC-owned networks such as USA Network (home of WWE SmackDown!), which are not available on fuboTV.DIRECTVStream live sports, breaking news and must-see shows, and enjoy up to $35 off your first month of DIRECTV.Free TrialWhat about ESPN Unlimited?ESPN Unlimited starts at $29.99 for full access to all ESPN channels as well as exclusive ESPN Unlimited coverage, but there is no free trial available. However, ESPN Unlimited can be bundled with Disney+ and Hulu for greater savings on all three services. Fans who have fuboTV or DIRECTV do not need ESPN Unlimited, because it is included with those services.ESPN UnlimitedSign up for ESPN Unlimited for $29.99 per month, or bundle with Disney+ and Hulu for greater savings.Sign up nowWWE WrestleMania 42 start timeWWE WrestleMania 42 starts at 6 p.m. ET/3 p.m. PT live on ESPN on both Saturday, April 18 and Sunday, April 19.There’s plenty more WWE coverage to be had throughout the weekend, however. Here’s the full can’t-miss schedule with WrestleMania start times from Friday to Monday.Friday, April 17WWE WrestleMania 42 Kickoff: 5 p.m. ET on ESPN2WWE Friday Night SmackDown!: 8 p.m. ET on USA NetworkWWE Hall of Fame 2026: 11:59 p.m. ET on ESPN UnlimitedSaturday, April 18Countdown to WrestleMania: 5 p.m. ET on ESPN2WWE WrestleMania 42 - Day 1: 6 p.m. ET on ESPN UnlimitedSunday, April 19Countdown to WrestleMania: 5 p.m. ET on ESPN2WWE WrestleMania 42 - Day 2: 6 p.m. ET on ESPN UnlimitedMonday, April 20WWE Monday Night Raw: 8 p.m. ET on NetflixWWE WrestleMania 42 cardThese are the matches that have been announced for WWE WrestleMania 42.
